definition.given: A signed-in user is viewing the loaded All products list in a phone-sized touch viewport. Product rows provide access to individual product details.
definition.when: The user swipes upward across a product row and releases the gesture.
definition.observed: The app navigates from the All products list to the detail page for the product row under the gesture instead of only scrolling the list.
definition.require: A swipe across a product row is treated as scrolling rather than opening the product. All products remains visible after the gesture ends.
allow: A movement threshold, gesture cancellation, scroll state, or delayed activation may distinguish tap from drag.
Taps, keyboard activation, or a separate details button may open product details.
Scrolling may be short, have momentum, or stop at a boundary while the drag retains the list context.

theory.title: Context-first mobile design - Touch interactions must accommodate finger input, movement, and unstable attention in mobile environments
theory.reference: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition, Chapter 6: Mobile Interfaces; designing-interfaces/chapters/ch06-mobile.md
theory.rationale: Vertical dragging is the primary browsing action in a narrow-screen long list. Scrolling gestures need sufficient tolerance and must cancel row clicks. Otherwise, users cannot safely browse because every small movement may send them to a detail page.

theory.title: Direct manipulation and action feedback - The visible result of a gesture must match the object the user is manipulating
theory.reference: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition, Chapter 8: Actions and Commands; designing-interfaces/chapters/ch08-actions.md
theory.rationale: Users drag list content and expect it to move with their finger. Interpreting the same gesture as navigation produces a completely different and unpredictable result. Reliable gesture cancellation preserves agreement between action and feedback.

reference_observation: After the upward gesture, All products remains visible instead of switching to a product detail page.
requirement_rationale: Merchants browse the product catalogue to review their inventory and open individual products when needed. On a phone, swiping across product rows is a normal way to browse the list; it should not be mistaken for choosing a product to open.
